reason: Selected controlled shortcut and reward experiments support checking tool necessity beyond final-answer correctness.

candidates.title: Reward tool necessity when cues drive unnecessary calls
candidates.rule: When RL-trained agents select tools from superficial prompt cues, compare a decision-level tool-necessity reward with answer-only training, using counterfactual cue tests.
candidates.passage: accuracy is preserved or improved relative to the no-cue baseline.
candidates.finding: The necessity reward suppresses cue-driven calls in the controlled setups while retaining task accuracy. Cue-tool semantic alignment and learned tool competence affect shortcut formation; dataset imbalance alone is insufficient.
models: GPT-5 Nano tool-necessity and correctness judge
workloads: Synthetic cue-injected Natural Questions, DeepMath, GSM8K and 2Wiki tasks
candidates.conditions: GRPO training in VerlTool; cues correlate with tools during training and are decoupled at evaluation.
candidates.limitations: Artificial correlations, one base model and an imperfect model judge. The apparent correlation threshold is setup-specific. Incorrect necessity labels can discourage useful calls; this is not a universal rule to minimize tool use.
candidates.validation_test: Compare answer-only and necessity-aware rewards on cue swaps, cue removal and genuine tool-required cases; measure unnecessary calls, accuracy, missed necessary calls and judge disagreement.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
